Definition: strictly froth at the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) fury (especially of God's displeasure with sin)
BiblicalUsage: Za'am is fury, most often God's fury against sin. Psalms 38:3 feels it in the body: "There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger." Isaiah 10:5 calls Assyria "the rod of mine anger," a nation God uses and then judges, and Jeremiah 10:10 says that at his wrath "the earth shall tremble." Lamentations 2:6 shows the same anger falling on Jerusalem itself when the feasts and sabbaths are taken away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's anger is not a mood but a settled opposition to evil, and I do not soften it. I hold that a God who never grew angry at cruelty, idolatry, and oppression would not be good, and the verses here show his anger falling on empires, on nations, and on his own people when they turn away. My position is that za'am should make me hate sin the way God hates it, and run to the mercy he offers.
